faq.q1: Are the jewelry pieces actually genuine vintage?
faq.a1: Yes, the jewelry is genuine. We inspect every item carefully during photography and packing to confirm its condition, so we are unable to accept returns or refunds for any damage reported after delivery.
faq.a2:
Japanese vintage jewelry is, in short, a category that rewards closer attention. Some pieces are built around precious materials such as Akoya pearls or Japanese coral, or finished with unique techniques like Shippo-yaki or Kutani-style decorative work.

What sets them apart isn't loudness. It's not quite Western fine jewelry. It's not quite Asian antique either. It sits somewhere in between, and that's precisely what makes it interesting.
faq.q3: Can I return or exchange an item?
faq.a3: We carefully inspect every item during photography and packing, so unfortunately we are unable to accept returns or exchanges for damage reported after delivery. To prevent item-switching, we do not accept returns under any circumstances. That said, we want you to feel confident before purchasing! If you have any questions or concerns, please don't hesitate to ask beforehand. We're happy to help!
faq.q4: So… where does orangekoko even source these things?
faq.a4: We source directly from private collectors and personal collections across Japan — jewelry chosen and cared for by one person, not mass secondhand inventory. Behind every piece is a story: who wore it, where it traveled, what it meant to them — and that story is part of what you're bringing home. Every piece goes through verification before it reaches you.
faq.q5: What's the current situation with their products?
faq.a5: A quick note before you fall in love with something: these are vintage pieces. That means small scratches, minor scuffs, and the occasional sign of a life well-lived are part of the package. If you're chasing perfection, this probably isn't your aisle. If you appreciate things that have actually been somewhere — welcome.
faq.a6: Aww, we totally get it — who doesn't love a good deal! Unfortunately our prices are fixed and we're unable to offer discounts. However, we do run special promotions from time to time, so stay tuned! But we promise every piece is carefully priced to reflect its quality and uniqueness! Hope you find something you love.
faq.q7: Wait, why was my order cancelled after I already paid?
faq.a7: Honest answer: some of our handmade and vintage listings are shared across multiple platforms simultaneously. If something sells elsewhere first, we may have to cancel — even post-purchase. We know, it's annoying. We're sorry. It happens. Listings can also disappear without warning for the same reason, so if you see something you love, don't sleep on it.
faq.q8: Are the measurements and photos reliable?
faq.a8:
Measured and inspected by hand, so there may be a millimeter or two of variance, or the occasional tiny detail we've missed. If condition matters a lot to you, feel free to message us first.

As for the photos — they're taken by us personally, so please do keep in mind that colours may vary slightly from the actual item depending on your screen and lighting conditions.
faq.q9: Why don't I need to worry about allergies or weird smells?
faq.a9: No pets in our studio — so zero fur, zero pet odours. And we genuinely cannot stand cigarette smoke, so there's absolutely none of that either.

returns.intro: Because every piece we sell is one of one — vintage, previously loved, and sometimes decades old — our approach to returns is built around the care we take before your order ships, rather than after.
returns.policyBody: Every item is carefully inspected, measured and photographed at the time of listing, so what you see is exactly what you'll receive. Because of this, and to protect the integrity of one-of-one pieces, we're unable to accept returns or exchanges once an order has shipped.
returns.beforeBody: We know buying vintage online takes a little trust, so we want you to feel completely confident before you check out. If you have any question at all — about condition, sizing, materials, or anything in the listing — message us first. We're always happy to share extra photos or details.
returns.issueBody: In the rare case your order arrives damaged in transit or doesn't match its listing, contact us within 48 hours of delivery with photos and we'll work with you to make it right.

brand.title: What orange means
brand.lead: Before anything else — a word about our name, and what ‘orange’ means to us.
brand.philosophy1: orange is not a color — it's a feeling. The moment afternoon light slows down. A quiet warmth that stays close to life without intruding.
brand.philosophy2: Not made to catch your eye, but to stay with you in the everyday. We believe jewelry doesn't need to constantly prove its presence. The best pieces simply accompany you in silence — leaving weight on the skin, leaving traces in time. That's where orangekoko begins.
brand.philosophy3: As a curated space, we seek out contemporary artisan works and vintage Japanese jewelry — not because they dazzle, but because they're worth wearing for years, worth returning to again and again.
brand.philosophy4: Craft, texture, a sense of time — these are our criteria. At orangekoko, jewelry is closer to a daily vitamin for living.
brand.philosophy5: Small, but necessary. Gentle, but taken seriously.
brand.closing: orange doesn't create impulse. orange leaves an impression.

about.expandedBody1: That's the version we put in writing. The real one starts with me: I've always loved Japanese vintage jewelry, and not the polished pieces sitting behind glass in a shop window. I mean the ones spread out table by table at some small-town flea market, the kind of place that never makes it into a guidebook.
about.expandedBody2: I go looking for them myself, and the best part is rarely the piece — it's the story that comes with it. The sellers are often the original owners, or their families, and they'll tell you where a piece traveled, who wore it and to what occasion, why it was finally set aside. Stories like that don't exist in big-city shops.
about.expandedBody3: What keeps surprising me is how well these pieces have survived. Japan has a quiet, deep-rooted habit of caring for things — mending rather than replacing, storing with intention, passing objects down instead of throwing them away. That habit of careful keeping is exactly why a piece from decades ago can still reach you in wearable condition, its history intact rather than worn away.
about.expandedBodyArtisan: Alongside these vintage finds, I've also started working with a handful of contemporary artisans whose pieces carry that same spirit — made in small batches, meant to be worn for years rather than a season, each one shaped by a maker's hand rather than a machine.
about.expandedBody4: That's what orangekoko is built on: pieces worth that kind of care, and the stories that come with them.
